note: Literature confirms prominent hyperkinetic movement disorders and episodic respiratory dysrhythmias (hyperventilation, sleep apnea) in RNU2-2-associated DEE.

evidence.text: Recurrent de novo RNU2-2 variants were identified in individuals with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and hyperkinetic movement disorders, highlighting spliceosomopathies in DEEs with hyperkinetic features.

source.title: Prominent Movement Disorders in RNU2‐2‐Related Spliceosomopathy
source.quote: We identified recurrent de novo RNU2-2 variants (n.35A > G and n.4G > A) in two patients with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and hyperkinetic movement disorders.

evidence.text: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE exhibit severe to profound impairment alongside distinctive respiratory dysrhythmias, including hyperventilation and obstructive sleep apnea.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (n = 3), and obstructive sleep apnea (n = 3).
